title: Deferential Promote Bridge with Cohort Lease and Automated Rollback
author: Sofia Martinez
description: Motivation: We need a promotion path that respects cohort ownership and avoids aggressive cutovers that cause user-facing regressions. This PR implements a 'deferential promote bridge' that (1) acquires a short-lived cohort lease before increasing traffic to a model variant, (2) runs parallel shadow validation for the cohort during a soft ramp, and (3) triggers automated rollback or hold when cohort-level SLO regressions or counterfactual regressions are detected. High level: orchestration controller + bridge runtime hooks + runbook wiring to Console. Design goals: preserve session affinity, reduce blast radius per cohort, enable fast automatic backout for transient regressions, and provide clear telemetry for post-mortem. Changes in this PR: new controller (promotebridge) that coordinates lease acquisition, shadow sample routing, and delta-safety checks; lightweight cohort-lease CRD with TTL; runtime hook to attach a short-lived shadow siphon to cohort requests; metrics and alerts emitted under rollout.promote_bridge.*. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-1982) - [x] Cohort lease CRD and controller - [x] Runtime hook and gateway routing change - [x] Telemetry metrics and dashboards - [x] Integration tests for lease lifecycle and rollback triggers - [x] Runbook and Console wiring - [x] Canary rollout tested in staging How it differs from existing promote controllers: instead of global fraction-based ramps this uses cohort-leases and an orchestrated soft ramp inside the cohort boundary. The bridge is 'deferential' because it yields to any active session-affinity constraints and avoids preempting other cohort leases. Rollback policy: immediate rollback if any of the following are observed within the grace window: cohort latency P95 increases > 30ms AND error rate delta > 0.5%; or offline regression detection on model outputs (semantic drift score threshold). On soft anomalies the controller will hold and widen shadow sampling for 10 minutes and re-evaluate. Migration/rollout plan: merge to main, deploy promotebridge controller to staging for 48h with two controlled cohorts (marketing-early, search-beta), then scheduled canary to 3 additional cohorts. Post-merge tasks: dashboard link, update operator docs, and announce on #deploys. Related linear items: ENG-1982 tracks follow-ups for tenant-configurable TTLs and telemetry cardinality. Rollout timeline: target GA in 3 weeks after staged validation.

release_notes: Introduces Promote Bridge: cohort-lease based promotion controller, shadow siphon for cohort-scoped validation, and automated rollback rules. Admins can configure lease TTL and shadow sampling caps via Console. Intended to reduce blast radius for canaries and speed safe rollbacks.
risk_mitigation: Default rollout disabled; operator flag 'enablePromoteBridge' must be set to true. Staged rollout plan restricted to opt-in cohorts. Alerts created for rollout.promote_bridge.rollback and rollout.promote_bridge.holdpoint. Added automatic mitigation to drain new cohort traffic and restore previous model snapshot on critical rollback.
